description: The bar chart compares the performance of five different models—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—on three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (Sentiment Acc.), STS Correlation (STS Corr.), and Paraphrase Accuracy (Paraphrase Acc.). The vertical axis represents the accuracy or correlation values, ranging from 0 to 0.8, with a scale marked at intervals of 0.2. The horizontal axis lists the model names. For each model, three bars are displayed side-by-side, colored light yellow for Sentiment Acc., light pink for STS Corr., and light blue for Paraphrase Acc. The legend in the top right corner identifies the color coding for each metric. The 2-Tier SimCSE model consistently achieves the highest values across all three metrics, with its STS Corr. bar reaching approximately 0.81, its Paraphrase Acc. bar at about 0.79, and its Sentiment Acc. bar at around 0.49. In contrast, the Single-task_baseline model shows the lowest performance, with its Sentiment Acc. at approximately 0.53, STS Corr. at about 0.50, and Paraphrase Acc. at roughly 0.79. The Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout and Unsupervised_SimCSE models show intermediate performance, with the latter generally outperforming the former in STS Corr. and Paraphrase Acc. while being slightly behind in Sentiment Acc. The bars for each model are grouped together, and the overall trend shows that the 2-Tier SimCSE model significantly outperforms the others, particularly in STS Corr. and Paraphrase Acc.
